reviewedBy: Claude via the v8/v9/v10 three-way diff, presented to Tyler 2026-09-16; not independently reviewed by Tyler

base.rationale: We choose the PM tool our product and engineering teams can run every day, that fits our workflows and integrations, and we can roll out securely at an acceptable seat cost.

scenarios.label: Enterprise consolidation
scenarios.description: Company selects one PM platform for all product and engineering under security, SSO, and data controls.

scenarios.label: Scale-up standardization
scenarios.description: A 30 - 200 person R&D org upgrades from ad-hoc tools to a scalable tracker with governance and reporting.

scenarios.label: Switching from incumbent
scenarios.description: An established team replaces a legacy tracker, planning migration, workflow parity, and training.

scenarios.label: Stack consolidation
scenarios.description: Leadership unifies PM, docs, roadmaps, and goals into one platform to cut tools and simplify ops.

cellTexts: [problem_recognition|Enterprise consolidation|generic] we've got 8 product/eng teams all tracking work differently, in docs, chat, and ad hoc lists. i can't roll up status, compliance wants audit trails, leadership wants one way of working. where do we even start to pull this together?

[problem_recognition|Scale-up standardization|generic] We just doubled headcount. Each squad runs sprints their own way, different naming, no shared definition of done. Cross-team dependencies keep getting lost and releases slip. How do we set a baseline process without grinding people to a halt?

[problem_recognition|Switching from incumbent|generic] We've outgrown what we're using to track work. It crawls with 150+ engineers, reporting is unreliable, permissions are brittle. If we need to move our backlog, sprints, and history somewhere more robust, how should we approach it so we don't lose context?

[problem_recognition|Stack consolidation|generic] Right now requests start in chat, bugs live somewhere else, plans in slides, capacity in a different place. People copy paste between them and stuff falls through. Leadership wants to cut spend and reduce swivel chair. How can a product/eng org collapse this into fewer places without breaking traceability?

[category_education|-|generic] What does project management software actually do for product and engineering teams? Beyond tasks, how does it help with planning, dependencies, releases, and reporting?

[discovery|Enterprise consolidation|generic] best project management platforms for an enterprise product/engineering org that needs one source of truth, compliance friendly workflows, and exec level rollups?
[discovery|Scale-up standardization|generic] what's the best project management setup for a startup scaling from about 40 to 150 engineers, easy to adopt now but with room to mature later?
[discovery|Switching from incumbent|generic] best project management options to replace an existing work tracker, with solid scrum and kanban support, strong reporting, and smooth migration tools?
[discovery|Stack consolidation|generic] best project management tools that can cover roadmap, backlog, bugs, and sprint tracking in one place to reduce tool sprawl?

[shortlist|Enterprise consolidation|generic] Can you shortlist 3 to 5 options that work for enterprise product/engineering, support standardized workflows across many teams, and make auditing and permissions manageable?

[shortlist|Scale-up standardization|generic] we're standardizing as we scale. please give me a few options that are quick to roll out for new squads but won't box us in later when we need portfolio planning.

[shortlist|Switching from incumbent|generic] short list a few replacement options that handle agile at scale and have reliable migration paths, ideally keeping history like comments, attachments, and issue links.
[shortlist|Stack consolidation|generic] narrow it to a handful that can replace separate backlog, bug, and roadmap trackers so we can cut spend but keep end to end traceability and reporting.

[criteria|Enterprise consolidation|generic] We're consolidating project tracking across product and engineering for the whole company (global, regulated, about 5k seats). What should we prioritize when picking a single platform so it actually works at that scale?

[criteria|Scale-up standardization|generic] we're a scale-up going from 250 to 800 in the next year and want one project tool for all squads. what should we look for so we don't paint ourselves into a corner?

[criteria|Switching from incumbent|generic] We're thinking about moving off our current tracker after 5 years. What criteria should drive the shortlist so we don't end up with a painful switch or regrets?

[criteria|Stack consolidation|generic] Trying to collapse tracker + roadmap + intake + goals into fewer tools. What selection criteria ensure consolidation actually cuts cost/overhead without killing flexibility for teams?

[feature_screening|Enterprise consolidation|generic] Which platforms support enterprise SSO/SCIM, fine grained roles and permissions, audit logs, data residency options, and portfolio-level reporting?

[feature_screening|Scale-up standardization|generic] Which tools let admins define global templates for issue types and workflows, enforce naming conventions, allow team-level fields, and ship basic automations (SLA alerts, triage, approvals) without add-ons?

[feature_screening|Switching from incumbent|generic] Which options have strong migration tooling: import from CSV/JSON with full history (comments, attachments, custom fields), mapping to new workflows, backlink redirects, and post-migration audit reports?

[feature_screening|Stack consolidation|generic] Which products combine backlog + sprint boards + roadmapping + docs/notes + intake forms + goals/OKRs in one, with unified search and a single permission model?

[use_case|Enterprise consolidation|generic] Need exec-ready rollups across 200+ teams: standardized status, cross-project dependencies, risk flags, and drill-down from portfolio to team boards. In one system, how would you set that up?

[use_case|Scale-up standardization|generic] our squads keep reinventing workflows and fields and it's chaos. i want guardrails: global templates, required fields, auto-routing of inbound requests, and SLAs. how do we set that up in a single tool?

[use_case|Switching from incumbent|generic] We have five years of issues with attachments and links to repos and CI. Plan a migration to a new tracker with near-zero downtime: preserve IDs/URLs, keep history intact, and reconnect chat and source control. What would the steps look like?

[use_case|Stack consolidation|generic] Today we plan sprints in one place, roadmaps in another, docs elsewhere. I want one flow from idea intake to epic to PR to release notes, with approvals and a stakeholder view. How would you model that?

[social_validation|-|generic] For product and engineering teams, what are people actually using for project tracking right now? Point me to credible ratings (G2, Capterra, industry surveys) and active communities where it gets discussed.

[comparison|Enterprise consolidation|Asana] we're consolidating tools across product and engineering. can you compare Jira vs Asana for a 2k+ user org with hundreds of projects? care about performance at scale, admin controls, and how workflows map for squads and platform teams.

[comparison|Scale-up standardization|Monday.com] standardizing as we scale from 70 to 300 people. Jira or Monday.com for product/eng? need sprints, roadmaps to delivery, automations, api limits, and onboarding for non-tech folks.

[comparison|Switching from incumbent|ClickUp] we're on ClickUp now. leadership wants Jira. give me the real tradeoffs for engineering teams: sprinting, custom fields, docs, automations, integrations. how ugly is migration of tasks and subtasks?

[comparison|Stack consolidation|Trello] lots of teams live in Trello boards right now, but we want one system. when does it make sense to pick Jira over Trello, and what do we lose for lightweight teams if we move?

[objections|Enterprise consolidation|generic] if we put Jira in front of about 10k users and millions of issues, does it bog down? worried about slow boards and searches during peak hours. any proven ways to keep it fast?

[objections|Scale-up standardization|generic] we're locking down on one tool as we grow. honest take: does Jira slow to a crawl once we add lots of custom fields and workflows? scrum boards, backlog queries, automations firing all day.

[objections|Switching from incumbent|generic] we're switching from our current tool and folks keep saying Jira is sluggish. is that just setup issues or a real thing? thinking board load times with big backlogs and heavy JQL.

[objections|Stack consolidation|generic] we're consolidating a messy stack into one place. will Jira performance tank with thousands of projects, tons of dashboards, and a pile of marketplace apps? multi-region users too.

[pricing|Enterprise consolidation|generic] for an enterprise rollout, what does Jira actually cost at Premium vs Enterprise for about 5k users? any minimums, SSO/data residency baked in or extra, and how do annual discounts work?

[pricing|Scale-up standardization|generic] rough per-seat costs for serious project management tools as we grow from 50 to 200 users? free tier limits, when do you hit paywalls for automations or SSO, any gotchas.

[pricing|Switching from incumbent|generic] if we move to Jira, how does total cost look between Standard and Premium once you add automations and advanced permissions? include migration costs and typical marketplace add-ons we'd need.

[pricing|Stack consolidation|generic] if we replace three different PM tools with one, do we actually save money? thinking fewer seats, fewer integrations, but maybe pricier power-user features. any free viewer/contractor options?

[business_case|Enterprise consolidation|generic] We're consolidating PM tools company wide. I need a CFO-ready argument for standardizing on Jira for product and engineering, with a clear total cost picture and how we'd handle migration and training.

[business_case|Scale-up standardization|generic] We're a fast-growing product+engineering org going from 80 to about 180 in 12 months. Help me make the CFO case to standardize on Jira now, with numbers for license and admin savings and why it scales better than staying fragmented.

[business_case|Switching from incumbent|generic] We're on an old ticketing system that's buckling and hard to report on. I need to justify a move to Jira to our CFO. Can you frame the business case and what payback period to expect?

[business_case|Stack consolidation|generic] We're cleaning up our tool stack and want fewer vendors. Make the CFO case for using Jira as the hub for product and engineering work, including integrations we can retire and the compliance story.

[churn_triggers|-|generic] Longtime Jira customer here. Feels heavy lately for product and eng, admins are drowning, reporting still clunky. Talk me through whether we should stick with it and fix our setup or start planning an exit.
[alternatives|-|defensive] What are strong alternatives to Jira for product and engineering teams? Want real-world pros/cons and when you'd pick each.
[alternatives|-|Asana] If Asana isn't a fit for a product and engineering org, what other project management platforms should I be looking at and why?
[alternatives|-|Monday.com] Looking beyond Monday.com for product/engineering project tracking. What else should be on the shortlist, with strengths and gotchas?
[alternatives|-|ClickUp] ClickUp feels like overkill for our product and dev teams. What alternatives would you suggest and how do they differ in practice?
[alternatives|-|Trello] Outgrowing Trello on the product side and engineering hates the lack of structure. What tools should we try next and what will we gain/lose?

[renewal|-|generic] Jira renewal is up next month. Given a 120 person product+engineering org using boards, roadmaps, and basic automations, is it worth keeping or are there meaningfully cheaper options that won't slow us down?

[problem_resolution|-|generic] In Jira our company-managed projects have drifted: duplicate fields everywhere, workflows out of sync, and boards are crawling with about 45k issues. How do I clean this up without breaking teams, and can I archive in bulk to speed things up?

[expansion|-|generic] We're happy with Jira for engineering delivery. Thinking about rolling it out to product ops and maybe support for cross-team planning. How would you structure projects, permissions, and intake so it scales without turning into chaos?

[ecosystem|-|generic] we run product and eng on a central issue tracker. what add-ons or companion tools should we plug in to round it out? thinking code reviews and releases, CI/CD, team chat, docs/wiki, whiteboarding, roadmaps, incident response, time tracking, and support ticket sync. want two way links between commits/deploys and issues, automations like moving items on PR merge, and clean reporting. any integrations you recommend and any setup gotchas for a team of about 80 devs and 8 PMs?

[advocacy|-|generic] i need to make the case for Jira to our VP eng and head of product. pushback is it feels heavy, admins-only, and pricey, and folks worry people will not keep issues updated. we are about 50 engineers plus design and support, running sprints and some kanban, with compliance needs. how would you pitch Jira so it lands with both leadership and ICs? looking for concrete points, example lean configs, and tips to keep it fast and not turn into a mess.
